summary: UCLA beat Colorado 28-16 at the Rose Bowl in Week 9 of the 2023 college football season, the only Pac-12 meeting between Chip Kelly and Deion Sanders. UCLA became bowl eligible at 6-2 despite four first-half turnovers, while Colorado fell to 4-4 after Shedeur Sanders was sacked seven times and the running game disappeared in the second half. The note includes a live-blog timeline, quarter scores, and broadcast details.
one_line: UCLA defeated Colorado 28-16 at the Rose Bowl, clinching bowl eligibility while Colorado dropped to 4-4 amid seven sacks of Shedeur Sanders.
key_facts: UCLA topped Colorado 28-16 at the Rose Bowl in the only Pac-12 matchup between Deion Sanders and Chip Kelly.
UCLA improved to 6-2 (3-2 in the Pac-12), clinching bowl eligibility.
Ethan Garbers, in his third start of the season, passed for 269 yards and two touchdowns for UCLA.
UCLA had four first-half turnovers, including two fumbles by Carson Steele, but none in the second half.
Shedeur Sanders threw for 217 yards and one touchdown and was sacked seven times, tying a season high.
Colorado finished with 38 rushing yards, its lowest total in a game this season; Sanders handed off only four times in the final two quarters.
Safety Shilo Sanders was ejected for targeting late in the first half after a hit on Carsen Ryan.
Travis Hunter, in his second game back from injury, recorded both interceptions of the game.
Colorado's only touchdown came on an 18-yard pass from Shedeur Sanders to Jimmy Horn Jr. with about two-and-a-half minutes left; its onside kick attempt was recovered by UCLA.
Colorado dropped to 4-4; two of its final four opponents, Oregon State and Utah, are ranked.
Colorado had not won in Pasadena since 2002.
Kickoff was 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 28, 2023, on ABC with Chris Fowler and Kirk Herbstreit calling the game.
UCLA's TJ Harden capped an 80-yard drive with a short touchdown run, and Collin Schlee added a seven-yard touchdown run to make it 28-9.
